title: CEO Interview with Dr. Gleb Tsipursky of Disaster Avoidance Experts
gist: Disaster Avoidance Experts CEO Gleb Tsipursky argues the bottleneck in enterprise AI is adoption, not licenses: many leaders bought AI without measurable productivity gains, and he sells behavioral-science-led workflow redesign with human review for high-consequence decisions, including in semiconductor firms.

insights.claim: Many leaders have bought AI licenses but cannot point to corresponding changes in productivity, quality or decision-making.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Spend on AI tools is outrunning demonstrable ROI, a risk for AI software revenue durability.
insights.quote: cannot point to corresponding changes in productivity, quality, or decision-making

insights.claim: Employees respond to AI unevenly: some are uncertain where it helps, some wary of errors or job impact, and others quietly use unapproved tools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shadow usage creates governance and data-leak exposure.

insights.claim: Customers worry about spending heavily without return, losing control of sensitive information, trusting inaccurate answers, and employees taking shortcuts supervisors cannot see.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: These are the buying objections AI vendors must answer.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Tsipursky says a technically capable AI solution can still fail to become standard practice, and that behavioral science helps diagnose why.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Adoption friction, not capability, may gate AI productivity gains.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

themes.theme: Staged trust and verification of AI decisions

insights.claim: For higher-consequence decisions, the firm builds in evidence checks, human review and escalation rules before scaling adoption.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Governance scaffolding is the precondition for delegating more work to agents.

insights.claim: Tsipursky would start semiconductor AI use with constrained tasks and expand authority only as evidence justifies it, because decisions on process recipes, equipment control or product disposition demand much stricter validation and authorization.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fab-floor AI autonomy will likely roll out slowly versus knowledge-work uses.
insights.quote: Decisions affecting process recipes, equipment control, or product disposition demand a much stricter validation and authorization process.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: A system can produce plausible recommendations that fail when operating conditions change, a concern for technical leaders.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Distribution shift risk argues for ongoing evaluation, not one-time validation.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: As agentic tools improve, habits of testing assistants on realistic examples, recognizing missing evidence and routing consequential decisions to reviewers will determine whether organizations can delegate more work safely.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Evaluation skill becomes a differentiator in agent deployment.
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

themes.theme: Semiconductor use cases for workplace AI

insights.claim: Tsipursky sees particular potential in semiconductor companies for engineering knowledge retrieval, cross-functional handoffs, training and analysis support.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Lower-risk, information-heavy tasks are the likely entry point for AI in chip firms.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: The firm's consulting spans midsize organizations and major enterprises, including Applied Materials, and it works within platforms clients have already approved rather than requiring a new AI vendor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral positioning targets spend already committed to AI tools.
